ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for all directors, shareholders, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners. Screening must be conducted before incorporation against FINTRAC policy standards, the PCMLTFA PEP definition for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and adverse media sources. Where any match or elevated risk arises, enhanced CDD measures, beneficial ownership attenuation analysis, source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval are required. Because the commercial model involves IVD manufacturing and SWIFT_LC / TT_WIRE payment rails, the risk tier is Medium_Risk_Enhanced and continuous AML/CFT monitoring must be maintained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Federal: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada online NUANS name search portal. Provincial (Quebec): Registraire des entreprises du Quebec / Quebec Enterprise Registrar, legal name reservation module.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Charter of the French Language, C.Q.L.R. c. C-11, requires a French legal name for corporations registered in Quebec. The official corporate name must be in French, or must have a French version that is registered and used in Quebec; English-only names are not permitted for commercial signange or for the registered name unless a statutory exemption applies. Transliterations of non-Latin script names into Latin characters are permitted, and the name must include a proper corporate suffix such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Incorporée', 'Corporation', or 'Société par actions'. A NUANS search is mandatory to verify that the proposed name is not confusingly similar to an existing federal, provincial, or territorial trademark or company name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant must first cure the grounds by submitting a revised name or by filing written submissions with the relevant registrar. For Quebec, a request for reconsideration may be filed with the Registraire des entreprises under the Enterprise Register Act, and any adverse decision may be challenged before the Superior Court of Quebec by way of judicial review. For a federal CBCA name refusal, the applicant may apply in writing to the Director appointed under the Canada Business Corporations Act for reconsideration within 30 days of the refusal, and may thereafter apply to the Federal Court for a judicial review of the Director's decision. During any appeal, the name protection is not extended unless a new reservation is obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office service providing a physical street address in Quebec and a person authorized to accept service of process may satisfy the registered-office requirement for a Quebec or extra-provincial corporation. However, for an ISIC 3250 / NAICS 334516 IVD manufacturing establishment, a virtual office alone is not sufficient commercial substance for Health Canada licensing, QST/GST registration, or CRA/Revenu Quebec audits. The company must maintain actual manufacturing or operational premises in Quebec or an applicable Canadian province before a Medical Device Establishment Licence can be issued.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High; approximately 85-90% within the first year after filing for a Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence under the Food and Drugs Act and the Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282. Revenu Quebec and the Canada Revenue Agency may also conduct unannounced premises visits for GST/HST and QST verification, payroll compliance, or corporate substance audits. The manufacturing facility must have physical inventory, equipment, records, and personnel at the registered address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c. S-31.1, ss. 16-37 (incorporation), s. 34 (share consideration), Part IV (organizational governance and directors); optional federal regime under Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44, not adopted.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Québec Enterprise Registrar, via the Services Québec/clicSÉQAT online business portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts de constitution) submitted with the Declaration of Registration (déclaration d'immatriculation).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; consideration fixed by the board. No escrow account requirement applies to IVD manufacturing corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that (1) the share subscription of [Incorporator] for 10,000 Class A common shares at CAD 1.00 per share, payable in full, is accepted; (2) the registered office of the Corporation is established at [Address], City of [City], Province of Québec, as of [Date]; (3) Bylaw No. 1 is adopted; (4) [Name A] is appointed Chair of the Board, [Name B] President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name C] Secretary and [Name D] Chief Financial Officer, each with authority delegated by Bylaw No. 1; (5) management is authorized to execute the REQ, Health Canada and environmental filings; and (6) all prior acts in furtherance of these resolutions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ — clicSÉQAT name search service (NUANS route)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed legal name for a distinctiveness check under QBCA s. 11; include both French and English variants; upon approval the REQ issues a name reservation valid for 60 days.
required_dossiers: NUANS report for the proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Refusal may be cured by consent letter from the conflicting holder, a revised distinctive element, or a fresh search; REQ notice must be answered within the prescribed period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ; draftsman: Quebec lawyer or notary (recommended)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statutory articles specifying share structure (Class A voting common, Class B preferred), permitted restrictions, Quebec registered office, and initial directors; the incorporator signs the articles; directors consent in writing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The REQ will issue an incompleteness notice; rectify the deficiency and refile; extend reservation if name expiry is imminent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing Articles, Registration and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the signed articles together with the declaration of registration and pay the statutory fee; the REQ issues the certificate of incorporation and the nine-digit NEQ; the certificate is obtained online immediately upon completion.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ rejects the filing, correct the cause of refusal and resubmit no later than the statutory deadline; in a contested refusal, apply to the Superior Court of Québec for rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Account Set-up with Revenu Québec and CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (Bureau des entreprises) and Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for GST/QST, payroll source deductions and corporation tax using the joint federal-provincial online registration; obtain the business number and Revenu Québec establishment file; open the corporate bank account under the certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Pending verification — supply the government notice with articles and lease; call the applicable support centre; amending the tax account after issuance requires a formal request to Revenu Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Meeting and Initial Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The Corporation — board of directors (QBCA s. 124)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first organizational meeting to adopt the first board resolution, approve share issuance and the share register, adopt Bylaw No. 1 and banking resolution, and appoint officers; record minutes in the statutory records register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director vacancy prevents quorum, the continuing board may appoint interim directors under QBCA s. 121(2) and validate resolutions at the next meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Zoning, Building and Operation Pre-Checks
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality; Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) for occupancy permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business permit and building occupancy authorization for the manufacturing address; confirm that the zoning allows IVD instrument assembly and cartridge production; arrange structural inspection where cleanroom or heavy equipment is installed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal an adverse municipal decision to the municipal council and thereafter to the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ); otherwise select a compliant site and restart the permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada — Medical Devices Directorate (MDD) of the Therapeutic Products Directorate; provincial industrial regulator: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) for manufacturing designation; workplace authority: CNESST.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) granted under s. 46(1) of the Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-282); production under ISO 13485 quality management certification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II — registration and sectoral declaration; the contained microfluidic/immunoassay production line is not a listed full-EIA activity, but a certificate or sectoral authorization for discharges is mandatory before commissioning.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: pH 6.0-9.5; BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L; suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L; residual chlorine ≤ 0.02 mg/L; bioreagent waste autoclaved at 121°C/15 min. Air: VOC capture ≥ 90%, VOC ≤ 250 mg/Nm³; no CFC/HCFC discharge; hazardous solids manifested under Recyc-Québec and transported by licensed carriers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the municipal fire safety service and RBQ compliance with the Building Code; structural load approval for cleanrooms and analyzer assembly; CNESST occupational health and safety clearance covering chemical, biological and electrical hazards, and mandatory prevention program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – federal GST/HST and Income Tax administration via My Business Account portal (www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html); Revenu Québec (www.revenuquebec.ca) – Quebec QST, payroll, and corporate tax administration. Business registration via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) and Revenu Québec SÉ@P portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A corporation incorporated in Canada automatically receives a federal Business Number (BN) (9-digit plus account identifiers). For a foreign-owned corporation, incorporate federally or provincially under Canadian business corporations law, then activate the BN via RC101 (online/paper) or BRO to obtain GST/HST, payroll, import/export accounts. For Quebec, register the corporation with Revenu Québec to obtain a Quebec Business Number (NEQ), then open a QST account (if threshold exceeded) using the same BN or with a distinct Quebec account identifier. Non-resident directors and shareholders are permitted; officers/directors residing in Canada are recommended but not mandatory under federal law; Quebec requires notice of directors. Retain CRA BN, QST account number, and NEQ for all invoicing and returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Canadian federal tax law. A Business Corporation is automatically a taxable Canadian corporation and pays federal and Quebec income tax at the entity level. Relevant statutory elections include: under ITA section 256(1), associated corporation definitions affecting the small business deduction; under ITA subsection 39(3) and related provisions, election to trigger capital gains/losses on deemed dispositions; and under Quebec Taxation Act, equivalent elections. For hybrid mismatch / interest limitation (EIFEL) purposes, an election is available under ITA subsection 18.21(3)(b) to recharacterize certain interest where deductibility was suspended on a non-consolidated basis; foreign entity classification is determined by CRA administrative policy, not elected by the taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Federal) and QST (Quebec) – destination-based value-added consumption taxes; combined effective rate applies in Quebec unless the supply is zero-rated (including exports).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada (and taxable supplies made in Quebec for QST) arising in a calendar quarter alone or in the four consecutive calendar quarters ending that quarter; a non-resident carrying on business in Canada is subject to this small supplier threshold. Once the CAD 30,000 threshold is exceeded, mandatory GST/HST and QST registration for taxable supplies made in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate in Canada; neither CRA nor Revenu Québec requires per-invoice digital stamping or continuous transaction controls (CTC). Electronic invoicing is permitted and the supplier must retain all invoices in a format that can be made available to the tax authority on request. GST/HST-QST returns must be filed electronically when total taxable supplies exceed CAD 1,500,000 or when registered for QST; Revenu Québec imposes mandatory electronic transmission of QST remittances and annual summary data. Invoices must meet information requirements under Excise Tax Act section 169(1) and Quebec QST provisions, including tax number, supply description, tax charged, and rate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of tangible goods manufactured in Canada (IVD cartridges, immunoassay analyzers, etc.) qualifies for 0% GST/HST and QST when the supplier transfers possession and ownership and delivers the goods to a location outside Canada (ETA section 6; Quebec QTA correspondingly). Goods shipped by common carrier with a destination outside Canada qualify if the supplier retains evidence of shipment. Related offshore services (installation, software licensing, calibration, or technical support) supplied to a non-resident not present in Canada may be zero-rated under ETA section 26 (services to non-resident) and Quebec equivalent, provided the services are not in respect of real estate in Canada nor any supply of goods made to the person while in Canada. The supplier must maintain contemporaneous documentation demonstrating the physical export and that no taxable Canadian use occurs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Customs Export Declaration (electronic ECI or B13A/R15 for controlled goods; otherwise validated commercial manifest or cargo control documentation)
Commercial invoice referencing the foreign purchaser, INCOTERMS, and destination of goods
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill) evidencing transport out of Canada
Packing list and if applicable Test Certificate / Certificate of Origin
Foreign Inward Remittance Advice or bank SWIFT credit advice from the Canadian clearing bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the ordinary course
For expedited export clearance, optionally Form A8A / CES-Decl with the carrier
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the normal four-year limitation period; where misrepresentation is attributable to neglect, carelessness, or wilful default, the period is unlimited. Failure to substantiate export zero-rating results in assessment of unreported GST/HST and QST at the standard rate, plus interest. Gross negligence penalties under ETA section 280.1 for false statements or omissions equal 25% of the understated tax; Quebec QST penalties apply similarly. False claims to obtain refunds (including export refunds) may attract criminal sanctions under ETA sections 381; and for corporate directors/employees, personal liability can arise in case of wilful participation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with prudential oversight by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and anti-money-laundering supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada adheres to IMF Article VIII. The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for current and capital account transactions. There is no central bank authorization requirement for inbound foreign direct investment or for the repatriation of dividends, interest, royalties, loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds to non-residents. Profit remittance is subject solely to federal and provincial withholding taxes (Part XIII of the Income Tax Act) and treaty relief. The Investment Canada Act imposes only national-security and economic-net-benefit notifications/approvals for certain foreign acquisitions, not exchange controls. Quebec imposes no supplemental convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation timeline exists for export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency balances in Canadian deposit-taking institutions or offshore accounts. Banks must file Large Cash Transaction Reports and Terrorist Property Reports to FINTRAC for cash/currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more. Export proceeds from IVD trade are treated as ordinary current-account receipts and clear on standard SWIFT rails without Bank of Canada intervention.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium for unregulated foreign EMIs. Canada requires any entity providing payment services to Canadian clients to register as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and to comply with the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) regulatory framework. Foreign digital EMIs may be used as supplementary payment channels for cross-border supplier settlements only if they hold a Canadian MSB registration, appoint a FINTRAC-compliant compliance officer, and cease collection/deposit activity that the law limits to chartered banks and credit unions. Dedicated deposit-taking and escrow accounts are not permissible for offshore EMIs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted under FINTRAC's risk-based approach for Canadian corporations, provided that directors and authorized signatories complete a video-based identity verification and the corporate records are verifiable through the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. However, for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced manufacturing entity with non-resident ownership concentration and a capital escrow account, major Canadian banks require at least one director or senior managing officer to complete a physical or hybrid KYC interview at a bank branch or before a Canadian notary/commissioner for oaths. The interview shall confirm beneficial ownership, source of funds, expected transaction profile, and export compliance measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership chain with an opaque intermediate holding vehicle located in a low-disclosure jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate ownership chart descending from the ultimate parent, share register with percentages, registered-agent certificates for each intermediate entity, notarized certificate of incumbency, and an AML questionnaire demonstrating the commercial purpose of the holding structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Automated sanction/PEP screening hit on a director, shareholder, or counterparty tied to a politically exposed person.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn declaration from the PEP confirming the non-pecuniary relationship, official corporate records isolating the affected individual from control of funds, an independent legal opinion that no sanctions list maintained by Global Affairs Canada, the UN, or OFAC screening is violated, and written consent to enhanced monitoring and periodic re-screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual inbound capital injection from a foreign parent without documented equity subscription or shareholder resolution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Quebec entity's corporate resolution approving the capital contribution, original/via SWIFT-received share subscription agreement, audited parent financial statements, bank statements evidencing the lawful accumulation of funds, and a tax-clearance certificate where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity on a newly opened account creates a pattern inconsistent with the stated IVD manufacturing business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Back-to-back purchase orders and sales invoices for microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers, bills of lading and customs declarations (including CUSMA certificates if applicable), manufacturer's export permits, and a treasury policy document explaining anticipated settlement cycles and jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registration of the company in Quebec with no Canadian-resident director raises governance concerns under the Canada Business Corporations Act default assumptions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Quebec counsel confirming that the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA) imposes no Canadian-resident director requirement, a certificate of corporate status from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, and a statutory declaration of the registered office and management authority.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or subordinated debt injections must be routed as SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or MT202 (interbank cover) to the Canadian beneficiary bank with the Quebec entity as named beneficiary. The payment instruction shall carry the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity capital) or 'LOAN' (intercompany loan) and reference the share subscription agreement, board resolution, and corporate registration number. Verification by the receiving bank will include full KYC of the beneficiary, source-of-funds documentation, and, for amounts exceeding CAD 10,000, mandatory FINTRAC reporting. The Canadian entity must also complete the quarterly Statistics Canada Balance of Payments (BOP) reporting if the inward remittance represents direct investment from a non-resident parent.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and operating disbursements will clear through SWIFT MT103/MT202 for cross-border wires, Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for domestic CAD clearing, and correspondent banking channels for USD (typically via the U.S. Clearing House CHIPS/Wire). For high-value IVD equipment and reagent inventory imports, an irrevocable, conformed Commercial Letter of Credit (ICC UCP 600) issued via SWIFT MT700 is recommended, with the Canadian bank acting as issuer/confirmer. All disbursements must be accompanied by the relevant commercial invoice, transport document, and certificate of origin where applicable, and must use ISO 20022 purpose codes consistent with goods and services trade (e.g., 'GDDS' or 'TRAD').
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNY) for firm transactional exposures
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for hedging exposures to currencies without local convertibility or deliverability, subject to bank credit approval
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term capital-exposure alignment on intercompany loans
Foreign exchange options (call/put) for protecting budgeted exchange rates on material procurement contracts
Exchange-traded futures and options on the Montréal Exchange or recognized Canadian/global exchanges for standardized CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/CNY instruments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration of Enterprise Registration (incl. beneficial-ownership dataset and registered-office confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of the enterprise registration with the REQ in each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statement of offence fines up to CAD 2,000 per non-compliance; failure to file for three consecutive years triggers administrative cancellation of the registration, loss of corporate name protection and legal publicity safeguards.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) - applicable only if the corporation is federally incorporated and registered extra-provincially in Quebec; N/A for a Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA) company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 100 per day of delay up to CAD 5,000 per filing; persistent failure may lead to administrative dissolution of the federal corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal; includes all mandatory CRA schedules and information returns for foreign affiliates and dividends paid)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; tax balance due within 2 months (3 months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeat failures raise the penalty to 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; compound daily interest accrues on overdue amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (CO-17) and related fiscal disclosures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; tax balance due within 2 months (3 months for a CCPC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months, escalated to 10% plus 2% per month for repeat non-compliance; daily interest at Revenu Quebec prescribed rates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) Annual Renewal for the IVD immunoassay analyzer and microfluidic cartridge manufacturing sites; note: the underlying Medical Device Licence for the devices has no annual renewal under the post-2014 Canadian regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of the establishment licence issuance each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew suspends or expires the MDEL; continued distribution of IVD devices without a valid establishment licence is an enforcement action under the Food and Drugs Act, subject to fines, injunction, device seizure and cessation of import or sale activities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based statutory audit threshold exists under Quebec or federal corporate law for a private corporation. An independent auditor is mandatory only if the corporation distributes shares to the public, is a bank or federally regulated financial institution, or public-interest rules apply. A unanimous written consent of all shareholders (QBCA or CBCA dispensation) waives the audit appointment for the financial year. For this private IVD manufacturer, the standard annual engagement is an unaudited review or compilation engagement under ASPE unless lender or shareholder covenants require a full statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; this private manufacturing company will default to ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) for its financial statements, with the option to elect IFRS if the foreign parent consolidates under IFRS. Financial statements are generally presented in Canadian dollars unless an eligible functional-currency tax election is made.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec: the annual REQ declaration must confirm and update every individual holding, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of voting rights or of the capital of the corporation, or exercising de facto control; any change must be filed with the REQ within 30 days of occurrence. Federal CBCA (if applicable): the Register of Individuals with Significant Control must be examined and reconciled at each annual shareholders' meeting, and any share-transfer-driven change in significant control must be recorded in the statutory registers within 15 days. Statutory registers must reflect all share transfers with board-approved transfer forms and share certificates before the annual declaration is certified.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (AGM minutes, board resolutions, transfer and issuance records)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control / Quebec UBO data record

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110 - 450 per year (CAD 150 - 600) for registered office address and corporate agent services in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,600 - 7,400 for an annual review engagement under ASPE (CAD 3,500 - 10,000); USD 11,000 - 33,000 for a full statutory audit if triggered by lender or parent requirements (CAD 15,000 - 45,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Quebec general corporate rate (15% Federal Part I general rate plus 11.5% Quebec general rate); reduced to 12.2% (9% federal plus 3.2% Quebec) on active business income up to CAD 500,000 for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) claiming the small business deduction.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED investment tax credit of 35% refundable on up to CAD 3,000,000 of qualified expenditures for CCPCs and 15% non-refundable for non-CCPCs; Quebec SR&ED credit of up to 30% refundable for SMEs; federal accelerated capital cost allowance for manufacturing and processing machinery; Quebec deduction for patent and IP commercialization revenues; 13% federal general rate reduction already embedded in the 15% federal headline rate; non-capital losses carry back 3 years and forward 20 years.
